Klimontow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Klimontów, Poland

Demolished. Jews settled in Klimontów after 1611, first under Opatów's kehilla before gaining independence by 1727; population reached 68.6% (1,318) by 1862. A 1940 ghetto held about 4,000 people (roughly 1,000 relocated from other towns); liquidated October 29, 1942, deporting residents via Sandomierz to Treblinka. This cemetery, likely established in the 18th century beside the synagogue, held a guard's house and, per 1929 community budget records, planned but never-built plans for a second cemetery on Osiecka Street. During WWII, individual and mass executions occurred here; in 1943, residents dug up a mass grave of 68 people murdered on November 30, 1942, searching for valuables, and desecrated a genizah (sacred-text burial site), using Torah fragments as shoe inserts. A 1950s school and sports field replaced the cemetery, with recovered bones reburied in a shared grave beside the field. The town's Memorial Chamber preserves items connected to writer Bruno Jasieński (born Wiktor Zysman) and other former Jewish residents.
